item.title: Oorja Bio Fibrosis Drug
item.description:
• Summary: Oorja Bio has launched with $30 million to advance an IPF (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) drug candidate originally from South Korea. The startup is developing a fibrosis candidate, as reported by BioPharma Dive and Fierce Biotech. IPF is a rare and progressive lung disease with high unmet need, and Oorja aims to bring new treatment options to patients.
  • MoAs: Antifibrotic mechanism (likely targeting TGF-beta or other fibrotic pathways; specific MoA not disclosed but candidate from South Korean biotech)
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, Fierce Biotech

item.title: Beam vs Wave AATD Editing
item.description:
• Summary: Beam Therapeutics and Wave Life Sciences are advancing gene-editing therapies for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD). A recent Biospace report highlights that Beam has shown promising efficacy, seemingly outperforming Wave in preclinical or early clinical data. Both companies aim to correct the underlying genetic defect in AATD, a rare liver and lung disease. The competition underscores the potential of in vivo gene editing to address monogenic disorders. Beam’s approach uses base editing, while Wave employs a combination of RNA editing and antisense oligonucleotides. The next readouts will be pivotal for determining which platform offers better durability and safety.
  • MoAs: Base editing (Beam); RNA editing/antisense oligonucleotides (Wave)
  • Sources: Biospace, Biospace
